function: RSU agent learns transmit beamforming and receive filter (beam prediction) and car agent configures the STARS, jointly improving radar SNR and in-vehicle user rate (pp. 4, 6).
system: ISAC RSU with 25 transmit and 25 receive antennas, single-antenna in-vehicle user, target-mounted STARS (simultaneous transmit and reflect) with 36 elements; band not stated (pp. 3, 9).
method: Multi-agent deep RL: MASAC (off-policy) and MAPPO (on-policy) actor-critic agents with fully connected layers; RSU and car agents learn by interaction on local observations (pp. 5-9).
data_channel: Custom simulated geometric channels (steering vectors, path-loss exponents 2.5 and 2.8) along a curved vehicle trajectory; no standardized channel model, dataset, or measurement (pp. 3, 9).
test_conditions: Agents learn and are evaluated in the same simulated environment; each setting (STARS size, antennas, power, speed 10-30 m/s, hyperparameters) is trained to convergence separately (pp. 9-12).
baselines: Learned only: MADDPG and MATD3 in the same framework, and a refraction-only STARS mode run with all four algorithms; no non-learned method (p. 10).
metrics: Average episode return, radar SNR, achievable rate (bps/Hz), and episodes to convergence (pp. 9-12).
q1_support: p. 9: "The path-loss exponents of the RSU-STARS and STARS-user". Custom geometric channel with steering vectors and a power-law path loss (page 3); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 11: "the average number of episodes required to converge four". Each scenario (STARS size, antennas, power, speed) is trained to convergence on its own; the paper never trains in one setting and tests in another.
q3_support: p. 10: "MADDPG [41] and MATD3 [42] algorithms within the". Only learned baselines are compared; the refraction-only STARS mode is run with the same learned agents; no random, fixed, optimization or EKF baseline appears.
q4_support: p. 12: "lightweight networks (3-4 FCs)" is only qualitative. No FLOPs, parameter count, complexity order or runtime is reported; Fig. 13 (page 11) gives training episodes to converge only.
q5_support: p. 9: "we provide extensive simulations to comprehensively evaluate". Self-built simulation with parameters in Table I; no code or data link or DOI and no public dataset; the only links in the paper are arXiv references.
notes: PDF is the arXiv version (arXiv:2311.10352v1) and carries no DOI, so the DOI-title match cannot be checked from the PDF; title and content fit an IEEE TVT 2024 paper on target-mounted STARS in ISAC vehicular networks. Area 5 rather than 3 because the MADRL designs RSU transmit beamforming and receive filter plus STARS coefficients for both radar SNR and user rate. q2 stays 0 because the sentence on page 10 about converged agent models in different scenarios is backed by Fig. 13, which counts episodes to converge in each scenario, so each one is trained separately. q4: only convergence episodes (Fig. 13) and fully connected depth (Fig. 17) are given.
